Reading and Spelling
A Trosnant reader has:
Excellent phonic knowledge and skills.
Knowledge of an extensive and rich vocabulary.
An excellent comprehension of texts.
Phonics and Spelling at Trosnant
In order to develop fluent early readers, we recognise that we need to use a systematic approach to teaching phonics. Consistent, high quality phonics teaching and learning plays a fundamental part in aiding the children to develop and apply the skills in all areas of the English Curriculum; this is achieved through the Monster Phonics programme. Daily lessons are delivered with enthusiasm and confidence to inspire progress amongst all our children at Trosnant.
Across Early Years and Key Stage 1, we use the Monster Phonics Programme which is a systematic, synthetic phonics programme for teaching phonics skills, starting with initial sounds, blending and segmenting. It also introduces children to ‘tricky’ words that cannot be decoded phonetically alongside high frequency words which are integral to building sight vocabulary. Each vowel sound has an animated, colourful character to stimulate children’s engagement and memory.
Meet the Monsters!
Monster Phonics has a clear philosophy:
As the children move into Key Stage 2, the children follow the Grammarsaurus Spelling Programme, which is personalised to suit the individual needs of our children at Trosnant. The spelling rules are applied and taught through a variety of engaging and fun activities. To develop the spelling expectations across the school we have a list of ‘Trosnant Non-Negotiables’, along with the year groups
Reading at Trosnant
We strive to enable our children to become fluent readers and promote a love of reading at Trosnant. Great importance is attached to enabling our children to become fluent readers. We strive to create a text-rich environment for all of our children which appeals to their varied interests. All children will be given the opportunity to read to an adult in school at least once a week. Children are expected to read at least 3 times a week to an adult at home, and this should be documented in each child’s reading diary and monitored weekly by the class teacher. Each child has a book which is in line with their reading level, as well as books from the library to read for pleasure.
Book Buddies is an opportunity for different year groups to mix and share their love for reading, as well as giving older children the opportunity to read and share their knowledge with the younger years.
Book Talk is taught weekly. We often link our text driver to other curriculum areas. This may be taught as group or whole class.
In Key Stage 2 children are introduced to the Scholastic Pro Reading scheme. Each child is assessed termly to inform a reading level. When a child has read a book, they complete a quiz about the book to develop comprehension skills.
All children are able to take a variety of fiction and non-fiction books home which they can access in our libraries. Each class has an allocated weekly library slot when they can exchange library books and undertake research.
Each year group have a ‘Trosnant Favourite Five’. These change termly and underpin a variety of genres. Throughout the term the children are given opportunities to immerse themselves in these rich texts during our reading sessions.
We have a reading reward system which continues to develop a love of reading. The children can climb the prize ladder, striving to reach the top prize; a ‘Golden Ticket’ to enter ‘Trosnant’s ‘Trove of Treasure’s’’!
This year for World Book Day we focussed on the book “The Day the Crayons Quit” and invited staff and children to come to school wearing one colour, effectively dressed as a crayon. The day was a great success.

On-site Nursery
Tops Havant is a day nursery & preschool based on our school site with whom we have a great working relationship. Tops provide Early Education and Care for children from the age of 3 months until they are ready to start school; they also run a holiday club and provide after school care for our 5-7 year olds.
We work closely with Tops to offer ensure our families receive high quality care and education for their families from 3 months until 11 years old, when we then continue to work closely with our partner secondary schools, helping to ensure successful transitions.
From Autumn/Winter 2025/26 there will be additional places available at the nursery with a Pre-school room in the school building. This will support smooth transition into school from TOPS nursery. Further information will follow.
If you would like to know more, visit the Tops Nursery’s using this link
Tops Nursery’s latest OFSTED Report can be found here
When making an appointment to look around our schools, if you would like to look around the nursery just let our office staff know.

Admissions
If you would like your child to attend our school, please see below our admissions policy for the current academic year and for the next academic year. You will also find a link to the Hampshire School Admissions web page. You can visit this page to make a Year R or Year 3 main round application, or to make an in-year application, to join any year group, at our school.
If you make an application for Trosnant through the in-year route it will be processed by our Admissions Officer. We will make contact with you via telephone and email. If we are unable to make contact our final contact will be via letter.
Parents/carers will be notified of the outcome of their application and the details about their right to appeal if needed. We aim to notify parents/carers of the outcome within 10 school days, and will have definitely notified parents/carers in writing within 15 school days, (as required by para 2.30 of the SAC).
If you need any further information, or would like to book a visit please call our Admissions Officer, Mrs Stradwick on 023 9247 5606.

Headteacher’s Welcome
Headteacher’s Welcome – Welcome to the Trosnant Federation!
Trosnant Infant and Junior Schools are thriving and popular schools, providing high quality primary education for all children and their families at the heart of the community in the Leigh Park area of Havant. This all begins with our excellent early years provision.
At Trosnant, our federation’s values are based on a positive ‘Growth-Mindset’ approach to life and learning. This means that we:
This is all underpinned by a culture of mutual respect. This is captured by our Values Tree:
As children progress through the schools, we build strong links with our local secondary schools, which ensures effective transition when the time comes for our children to move on to the next stage of their education.
We also benefit from having an independent local Nursery on our site, working in close partnership with them to ensure a successful and happy transition for those children joining our infant school from the beginning.
We are proud of our school, it’s evolving, exciting and engaging curriculum, effective and engaging teaching, our focus on core skills and the offer of a wide range of unique opportunities.
The staff and governors have high expectations for our children ensuring everyone can achieve their best, within a caring, nurturing and inclusive environment, which recognises the individuality of each child.
Our schools have a wide range of well qualified staff, which includes:
all of whom work alongside the classroom and administrative staff to ensure the needs of all our children are well met.
We also commission services to provide our federation with mental health support and counselling, educational psychology and speech therapy.
We have a long history as schools who care for the ‘whole child ‘and their families. We provide an early bird breakfast club for working parents, morning bagels for any child who needs it to start their day well, and a range of after school clubs. We provide after school care in partnership with Tops Nursery and Barncroft Primary School.
I hope this website gives a good insight into our schools, and provides you with plenty of useful information. However, if you are considering choosing our schools for your children, or have been given a place here, please contact us if you require further information, have any queries or questions, or would like to arrange to visit us. We look forward to welcoming you and your children.
Ian Waine BA(Hons) – PGCE NPQH MSc

Parents
Here at the Federation of Trosnant Schools we believe that parents are partners in their child’s education. Creating a love of learning and an appreciation of its importance is the central idea behind family learning. Storytelling Club is a great example of giving our parents the opportunity to start the day reading a good book with their child before the school day gets under way.
Important dates
School dates for the 2025/26 academic year can be viewed here.
Inset days agreed for the new academic year:
Should we have to close the school due to adverse weather conditions, we will always inform our parents as quickly as possible, along with notifying Hampshire CC who will update their school closures. You can check on any changes by following this link to Hampshire CC.
If you require a 2nd copy of school communications, please contact the school office to discuss your requirements. Please ensure that all contact details are kept up to date by informing the school office of any changes. All letters are also regularly posted on this website. Please also contact the school office should you require any paper copies of the website or the contact contained therein.
3rd September 2025
6th October 2025
20th July 2026
21st July 2026
22nd July 2026
School uniform
School branded uniform can be ordered online with Brigade by clicking here or can be purchased from Skoolkit in their shop in Havant or online here. We hold sample sizes in the school office that you are welcome to use as a guide for ordering. We also have a range of good quality, second hand uniform items available to purchase from the school office at just 50p per item.
It is not essential to wear uniform items with the school badge displayed and as such you could also purchase items from the school uniform departments of any shop or supermarket.
New Year R children starting school in September 2025
For all those children that started school with us in Year R in September 2025, we hope that you have all returned your registration forms and any other necessary paperwork. It is your legal duty to complete all of the necessary paperwork before your child commences school with us.
All infant school children are entitled to free school meals, so please encourage your child to choose from one of our 3 options daily once they are staying for lunch. If your child has allergies please speak to a member of our office team who can assist with this.
Applying for a school place in September 2026
If your child is starting school (Year R) in September 2026, or transferring to Junior School (Year 3), the main application rounds will open in November 2025. More details will be given in due course.
For our Year 6 children transferring to secondary school in September 2026, the main application round will open in October 2025.
Please click here for a link to Admissions at Hampshire CC where you can access all the up to date information on making a school application for your child.
Assemblies
Every Monday we hold a Federated assembly with the whole school. Details of the assemblies for the autumn term will be posted here soon.
School Nursing Service
The School Nursing Service work very closely with schools across Hampshire and can support parents on a range of topics. They run a clinic once a month within our Hut and Trosnant parents/carers can book in for this through our family support workers, if they feel they need any support from the school nursing team. To find out more information on what they offer click here.
Tops Day Nursery
We are very lucky to have on site Tops Day Nursery who offer high quality childcare for children aged 3 months – 8 years old. Every 15 minutes is important and your time is valuable, that’s why they offer flexible childcare, so you only pay for time you need.
Tops will care for children from 3 months to schools age and they are open from 6.30am – 7.00pm. The nursery offers a safe, stimulating environment for all ages by qualified and friendly staff. Visit their website for more details.

Attendance and Opening Hours
At the Federation of Trosnant Schools we place a high importance on attendance and fully believe in ‘everybody in school, on time, every day’.
Research shows there is a clear link between good school attendance from an early age, with success later in life at GCSE study, university and during careers.
OFSTED suggest that attendance should be a minimum of 96%.
Why Attendance Matters
Research shows that poor attendance doesn’t just affect school results—it can impact future earnings and job prospects. Studies suggest that each additional day missed in secondary school can reduce lifetime earnings by around 0.8%, and students with strong attendance are more likely to access higher education and skilled employment.
Good habits now build routines, resilience, and social skills that last a lifetime.
Thank you for working with us to give every child the best chance to succeed—both now and in the future.
Book appointments outside school hours where possible.
School Opening Hours
The school is open from 8.30am and registration is at 8.45am. Learning activities are provided from 8.30am and this gives a calm start to the day as staff are able to settle the children and speak to parents about ant worries or concerns. Children are late if they arrive after 8.45am. School closes at 3.15pm.
The DfE expectation for all state-funded schools is a minimum 32.5-hour school week. Trosnant Federation provides 33 hours 45 minutes per week, which is 1 hour 15 minutes above the minimum expectation.
Unauthorised absences
In accordance with government policy, from September 2015, Hampshire County Council introduced measures for dealing with unauthorised absences. In particular they brought in fines across the county where a child’s unauthorised absence was 10 sessions (5 days) or more in a 10 week period. Fines are set at £80 per parent, per child. Hampshire County Council have issued an information leaflet about the penalty notices and it can be viewed here. Parents should be aware that a late arrival after 9.15am will be marked as an unauthorised session for the morning.
Our Headteacher is required to follow the local authority policy in respect of authorising absence and issuing penalty notices where applicable, for further information on our school attendance processes please click here.
We aim to work in close partnership with families to ensure all our children have good attendance. Further information is available on the Hampshire Education Website.
Please find see the following link to the school term dates as set by Hampshire so that you can ensure you are booking holidays outside of term time. If you are unsure please contact the school office before booking a holiday. There are occasions when absences might be authorised in exceptional circumstances.
If you need help with, or are worried about, your child’s attendance, please contact the office and ask to speak to one of our Family Support Workers, who can offer advice and support.
You can also find useful information on attendance and managing illness on this government managing illness blog – click here
There are also some useful videos available online explaining why good attendance is important for your child and giving tips on how you can help. You can find these videos here
We work closely with schools in the local area to ensure we all follow the same procedures and processes.

Home School Agreement
At Trosnant the learning partnership between school and home is recognised as being vital in ensuring all children achieve their best. There is a ‘Home School Agreement’ (as shown below) shared with all new families, which defines the role and responsibilities of parents, children and the school and is available from the main office.
The schools welcome parents into school both formally and informally to support their children’s learning and development which opportunities for family learning where parents and children learn side by side. Alongside this children have a range of home learning activities, of which reading is at the core.
The schools have an ‘open door’ policy, encouraging parents to discuss any worries, concerns, or just to ask questions, with both classroom and senior staff.
Year R send out a weekly newsletter with photographs to keep the parents up to date
